properties.natural_language: Before beginning the validation sequence via EDGE-START-VALIDATION, the EVMC call message received from the Ethereum client must contain a valid EVMC message structure with defined message type, destination address, and code fields
After message type validation fails (type != EVMC_CALL), the system must transition to STATE-MESSAGE-TYPE-INVALID and return EVMC_REJECTED, never proceeding to destination validation
The validation sequence must always follow strict ordering: message type check, then destination address check, then code check. No validation step may be skipped or reordered
Before validating the destination address, the destination must be checked against EIP-1352 precompile address ranges (0x01-0x09 for current precompiles)
When the destination address is not a precompile, the system must emulate empty code execution returning EVMC_SUCCESS with full gas intact and empty output
Before executing a precompile, the code argument must be NULL and code size must be 0; any non-null code must be rejected
The EVMC module must use ABI version 6 as specified; any ABI version mismatch between client and module must be detected and rejected
Before gas cost calculation, the precompile must have passed all validation checks and be in STATE-PRECOMPILE-READY
After gas check determines cost > limit, the system must return EVMC_OUT_OF_GAS with zero remaining gas and must not execute the precompile logic
Gas remaining after successful execution must equal gas_limit minus gas_cost, and must be non-negative
After precompile execution failure (non-gas reason), the system must return EVMC_FAILURE and no output data
The EVMC result must be exactly one of: EVMC_REJECTED, EVMC_OUT_OF_GAS, EVMC_SUCCESS, EVMC_FAILURE, EVMC_REVERT, or empty code result. No other status codes may be returned
When EVMC_REVERT is returned, the unspent gas must be preserved and returned to the caller, unlike EVMC_FAILURE which consumes all gas
The host interface (evmc_context) being NULL must not cause crashes during precompile execution since precompiles should not require host access
Before the identity precompile begins execution, the calling contract must have provided a valid CALL to address 0x04 with sufficient gas for at least the base GAS_IDENTITY cost
After identity precompile execution completes, evm.output must be byte-for-byte identical to evm.message.data input
The identity precompile must never modify, transform, or filter input data; it is a pure pass-through operation
After gas charging, the gas deducted must equal exactly GAS_IDENTITY + GAS_IDENTITY_WORD * ceil32(len(data))/32
Before gas deduction, the input length must be correctly measured and rounded up to the nearest 32-byte boundary via ceil32()
After gas deduction fails, the operation must halt with an out-of-gas error and no output data must be returned
For zero-length input, the gas cost must be exactly GAS_IDENTITY (base cost only, with zero word count), and output must be zero-length
Before processing external data through the identity precompile, the system must accept that input is untrusted and arbitrary; no format or content validation is performed
The identity precompile output must always be treated as untrusted by the calling contract, since it performs no validation on input data
Memory allocation for copying input to output must be bounded by gas costs, preventing resource exhaustion from large inputs

Before gas calculation begins, the ModExp precompile must receive a call to address 0x05 with calldata containing base_length, exponent_length, and modulus_length encoded as 32-byte big-endian integers
After multiplication complexity computation, the result must equal ceil(max(base_length, modulus_length) / 8) squared
After final gas cost computation, the result must be at least 200 (the minimum gas floor) regardless of input parameters
The GQUADDIVISOR must always be 3 in the final gas formula: gas = max(200, floor(complexity * iteration_count / 3))
When exponent_length <= 32 and exponent equals zero, the iteration count must be 0
When exponent_length > 32, the iteration count must equal 8*(exponent_length - 32) + bit_length(exp_top_256_bits) - 1, with minimum value of 1
The iteration count must always be at least 1 for non-zero exponents, ensuring gas is charged for actual computation
Before ModExp execution proceeds, gas must be verified sufficient via EDGE-HAS-GAS; insufficient gas must result in out-of-gas without executing the computation
After successful modular exponentiation, the result must equal base^exponent mod modulus, and be returned to the calling context
The minimum gas floor of 200 must always be applied, even for trivial inputs where the computed gas cost would be less than 200
Before processing any ModExp call, the gas cost computation must complete to prevent DoS attacks from potential attackers sending cheap trivial inputs
Gas cost must accurately reflect actual computation time across all client implementations; gas underpricing relative to computation time creates DoS vectors
Before a proposal can be classified, it must be submitted by a proposal author via EDGE-SUBMIT-PROPOSAL with a valid proposal draft document
After classification as a core protocol change, the proposal must receive an even EIP number and be routed to the EIP repository
After classification as an application layer change, the proposal must receive an odd ERC number and be routed to the ERC repository
Every proposal must be classified into exactly one category: core protocol change OR application layer change. Proposals spanning both must be split
Before URL migration check, a user must request a legacy ERC URL at eips.ethereum.org domain
When a migrated ERC is requested at the legacy URL, an HTTP redirect must be issued to the equivalent path at ercs.ethereum.org
When an EIP resource is requested, it must be served directly from eips.ethereum.org without redirect
Redirect infrastructure must remain operational indefinitely to support legacy URLs until all external references are updated
Before WS checkpoint validation, the node operator must provide a checkpoint via CLI in the format 0x<32-byte-hex>:<epoch_number>
After parsing, the checkpoint must yield a valid 32-byte block root and a valid epoch number; malformed input must be rejected
When checkpoint epoch > finalized epoch and block is not found in canonical chain, the client must emit a critical error and terminate
When checkpoint epoch <= finalized epoch and block root does not match canonical chain, the client must terminate with a descriptive critical error
A successful WS checkpoint validation must always result in STATE-WS-CHECKPOINT-VALID; a failed validation must always terminate the client with no partial operation
Before computing the weak subjectivity period, the beacon state must provide accurate validator count, average balance, and churn limit parameters
When current_epoch exceeds checkpoint_epoch + ws_period, the safety margin must be considered degraded and the checkpoint must be refreshed
Within the weak subjectivity period, the minimum slashing threshold for a long-range attack must remain at least 1/3 - SAFETY_DECAY/100 (approximately 23.3% with SAFETY_DECAY=10)
The WS period computation must use Ether (not Gwei) to avoid uint64 overflow in arithmetic operations, using floor division for Gwei-to-Ether conversion
Before a long-range attack can succeed, an attacker must control historical validator private keys representing at least 1/3 of the total stake
When conflicting finalized checkpoints are detected, at least 1/3 of the total stake must be identified as slashable for creating the conflict
When a WS checkpoint is used to evaluate conflicting chains, the client must reject the attacker's fork and remain on the correct canonical chain
The weak subjectivity checkpoint must be from a trusted source on the canonical chain; a checkpoint from an attacker's fork permanently compromises the node
Before tracking state changes, the world state trie must be loaded from persistent storage into memory
After a transaction succeeds, all tracked state changes must be committed atomically to the world state trie with no partial commits
After a transaction fails, all tracked state changes must be completely rolled back to the pre-transaction state with no residual modifications
The state tracker must capture all state modifications completely; incomplete tracking could result in state corruption on rollback
Before access list processing, a transaction with access list must be received from the external user via EDGE-USER-SUBMIT-ACCESS-LIST-TX
After access list parsing, all addresses and storage keys must be marked as warm in the access set, reducing subsequent access gas costs
All clients must implement consistent access list gas pricing to prevent transaction execution discrepancies across implementations
Before block processing, a block must be received from a network peer via EDGE-PEER-SUBMIT-BLOCK with valid block header and body
After block structure validation passes, the block must proceed to bloom filter computation and state trie update
The bloom filter must correctly index all log topics without false negatives; missing entries would cause dApps to miss critical events
After state trie update, the Merkle-Patricia trie must reflect all transaction-induced state changes for the block
Before fork activation, the block timestamp must equal or exceed the scheduled activation timestamp for the target network
After fork rules are applied, the fork identifier must be updated to the network-specific value (e.g., 0x5167e2a6 for Mainnet)
All 11 core EIPs and 4 supplementary EIPs must be applied atomically during fork activation; partial application would break consensus
Timestamp synchronization across distributed nodes must be sufficient to avoid disagreement on fork activation timing, preventing temporary chain splits
BPO forks must activate in strict sequential order: BPO1 before BPO2 before BPO3, with each requiring the previous to be active
After each BPO fork activates, blob capacity parameters must be updated to the new values and the network must operate under the new parameters
Before each BPO timestamp-triggered activation, the block timestamp must have reached the specific BPO activation timestamp
EIP inclusion scheduling must follow the state machine: PROPOSED -> EVALUATED -> (CONSIDERED -> SCHEDULED | DECLINED). No transitions from DECLINED back to CONSIDERED are permitted
Consensus must exist across all client teams regarding included EIP changes; implementation differences could cause network partitions
Before ECRECOVER execution, a CALL must be made to address 0x01 with at least 128 bytes of input data (message hash, v, r, s); shorter input is zero-padded
After successful key recovery and address derivation, the output must be a 32-byte value with the 20-byte address left-padded with 12 zero bytes
When validation fails or recovery fails, the precompile must return empty output (no data) rather than reverting the call
ECRECOVER must always terminate in STATE-ECRECOVER-COMPLETE regardless of input validity; it must never hang or loop
Before key recovery, v must be exactly 27 or 28, r must satisfy 0 < r < SECP256K1N, and s must satisfy 0 < s < SECP256K1N
When v is neither 27 nor 28, validation must exit early with empty output without checking r or s
Validation must follow strict sequential order: check v first, then r, then s. Any failure at any stage must result in early exit with empty output
Before processing, all signature data from the calling contract must be treated as untrusted input crossing a trust boundary
The cryptographic bounds validation must prevent signature malleability by ensuring r and s are within the curve order
The secp256k1_recover cryptographic library must be correctly implemented; faulty recovery could allow signature forgery or return wrong addresses
Keccak256 must be collision-resistant for deriving addresses from public keys; address collisions would enable impersonation attacks
Before a binary comparison operation, the EVM stack must contain at least 2 values; stack underflow must raise StackUnderflowError
After any comparison operation, the stack must have exactly one fewer element than before (two popped, one pushed), with the result being U256(0) or U256(1)
Comparison results must always be exactly U256(0) for false or U256(1) for true; no other values are permitted
The first popped value must be treated as the left operand and the second as the right operand; reversing operand order would produce incorrect comparison results
Signed comparison operations (SLT, SGT) must correctly handle 256-bit two's complement representation; incorrect conversion would produce wrong control flow
After comparison instruction completes, the program counter must be incremented by exactly 1
All five comparison operations (LT, GT, SLT, SGT, EQ) must dispatch from STATE-OPERANDS-LOADED with mutually exclusive opcode selection
Before ISZERO execution, the EVM stack must contain at least 1 value; stack underflow must raise StackUnderflowError
After ISZERO with value == 0, U256(1) must be pushed; after ISZERO with value != 0, U256(0) must be pushed
ISZERO must maintain stack depth: one value popped, one value pushed, net change of zero
Before executing any comparison instruction, GAS_VERY_LOW must be charged; insufficient gas must halt execution with out-of-gas
After gas exhaustion during comparison, execution must halt completely with no state changes from the comparison applied
All comparison opcodes (LT, GT, SLT, SGT, EQ, ISZERO) must consume exactly GAS_VERY_LOW gas; no comparison operation has variable gas cost
After an epoch transition, the beacon_finalized_epoch gauge must be updated to reflect the current finalized epoch number
After an epoch transition, both beacon_current_justified_epoch and beacon_previous_justified_epoch gauges must be updated
After an epoch transition, validator count metrics must reflect the current active, pending, exited, and withdrawable validator counts
After fork choice runs, beacon_head_slot must be updated with the latest chain head slot
When a chain reorganization is detected during fork choice, the beacon_reorgs_total counter must be incremented
Metric collection overhead must be negligible relative to consensus processing time to avoid performance degradation on critical path operations
After a peer is added or dropped, the libp2p_peers gauge must be updated to reflect the current total connected peer count
When a gossip message fails validation, the libp2p_pubsub_validation_failure_total counter must be incremented
The Prometheus metrics endpoint must be accessible only to authorized monitoring infrastructure; unauthorized access would enable information disclosure about node health and topology
Before data column processing, a data column sidecar must be received and submitted for gossip verification
After KZG batch verification and inclusion proof verification both pass, the data column must be marked as verified and the success counter incremented
Data column verification must follow strict ordering: gossip processing, then KZG batch verification, then inclusion proof verification. No step may be skipped
After data column verification succeeds, missing columns may be reconstructed from available ones, with reconstruction time and count tracked by metrics
Metric types must be semantically correct: counters must be monotonically increasing and gauges may fluctuate; incorrect metric type assignment would produce misleading monitoring data
